\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Serialization as a transition table]
\lean{Turing.CodeNDTM.serialize_eq_tableBitsK}
\label{Turing.CodeNDTM.serialize_eq_tableBitsK}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.CodeNDTM, Turing.CodeNDTM.serialize, Turing.NDTM.fixChoice, Turing.actionBits₂_eq_actionBitsK, Turing.codeTable2Bits, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.tableBitsK, Turing.tableBitsK_two, Turing.unaryFin}
\difficulty{3}
For every machine $M$ in code normal form, its serialization is the pairing of the
binary representation of its state bound with the unary encoding of its initial state
followed by the two transition tables, in order: the table for choice $0$ and then the
table for choice $1$. Each table lists the actions for all states, input readings, and
work-tape readings.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Replay Machine Serialization]
\lean{Turing.exists_replayCanonizer}
\label{Turing.exists_replayCanonizer}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.NDTM.replayTM, Turing.serializeK}
For every effective code system $c$ for two-work-tape nondeterministic binary machines,
there are a finite-state deterministic binary machine $M$ and a function
$T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every binary string $\alpha$, $M$ computes in
time $T(|\alpha|)$ the fixed serialization of the deterministic replay machine obtained
from the machine decoded from $\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Interpreter for Nondeterministic Machines]
\lean{Turing.exists_ndInterpreterCore}
\label{Turing.exists_ndInterpreterCore}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.CodeNDTM.toFinNDTM, Turing.EffectiveNDMachineCode, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.NDTM.initCfg, Turing.NDTM.runWith, Turing.pairEncode}
For every effective code system $c$ for two-work-tape nondeterministic binary machines,
there are a natural number $K$, a finite state set $Q$, a deterministic binary machine
$R$ with $K$ work tapes, a work-tape index $j$, and states
$\mathrm{entry},\mathrm{accept},\mathrm{reject}\in Q$ with
$\mathrm{accept}\ne\mathrm{reject}$ such that the following holds. For every binary code
$\alpha$, there is a constant $C$ such that for every binary input $x$, time bound $t$,
and choice string $s$ with $t\le |s|$, let
$z=\langle\langle\operatorname{bits}(t),\alpha\rangle,x\rangle$, let $N$ be the machine
decoded from $\alpha$, and let $e$ be the configuration obtained by running $N$ on $x$
for the first $t$ choices in $s$. Starting $R$ on input $z$ in state $\mathrm{entry}$,
with tape $j$ containing $s$ and all other work tapes blank, there is a time $T$ with
$T\le C(t+1)$ at which $R$ is in state $\mathrm{accept}$ if and only if $e$ is halted
with output $[1]$, and otherwise is in state $\mathrm{reject}$; neither state occurs at
any earlier time. Moreover, for every $t'\le t$ such that the run of $N$ using the first
$t'$ choices of $s$ is halted, $T\le C(t'+|x|+|\operatorname{bits}(t)|+1)$.
\end{theorem}
